concepts.title: Universal Adult Franchise and Democratic Consent

Explain in your own words what 'Universal Adult Franchise and Democratic Consent' refers to.
questions.a: The democratic entitlement granting every mature citizen the prerogative to participate in political elections without discrimination.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Universal Adult Franchise and Democratic Consent'.
questions.a: Democratic authority originates directly from the consent and collective electoral choices of the citizenry.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Universal Adult Franchise and Democratic Consent', in plain ASCII form.
Explain in your own words what 'Representative Democracy and Legislative Delegation' refers to.
questions.a: A governance structure wherein the populace does not rule directly but delegates policy decisions to elected deputies.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Representative Democracy and Legislative Delegation'.
questions.a: Citizens direct and supervise governance through representatives chosen from distinct territorial constituencies.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Representative Democracy and Legislative Delegation', in plain ASCII form.

Explain in your own words what 'Lok Sabha Majority for Government Formation' refers to.
questions.a: The mathematical threshold of elected legislators a political party or coalition must secure to establish the national executive.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Lok Sabha Majority for Government Formation'.
questions.a: Executive authority requires commanding more than half of the elected membership of the lower house.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Lok Sabha Majority for Government Formation', in plain ASCII form.
Explain in your own words what 'Coalition Government Formation' refers to.
questions.a: An alliance formed by multiple political factions when no single party secures an absolute legislative majority.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Coalition Government Formation'.
questions.a: Distinct political groups unite around common priorities to meet the executive threshold.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Coalition Government Formation', in plain ASCII form.

Explain in your own words what 'Composition of Rajya Sabha' refers to.
questions.a: The aggregate tally of members constituting the Council of States through indirect state election and presidential nomination.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Composition of Rajya Sabha'.
questions.a: The upper house combines state-elected representatives with distinguished presidential nominees.

Explain in your own words what 'Parliamentary Oversight via Question Hour' refers to.
questions.a: The formal opening interval of legislative sessions allowing lawmakers to interrogate ministerial functioning and policies.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Parliamentary Oversight via Question Hour'.
questions.a: Questioning executive officials keeps the ministry vigilant and accountable to public interests.

Explain in your own words what 'Constitutional Function of the Opposition' refers to.
questions.a: Legislative parties remaining outside the governing coalition tasked with scrutinising executive proposals and offering alternatives.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Constitutional Function of the Opposition'.
questions.a: An active opposition curbs unilateral executive actions and mobilises public consciousness on national issues.

Explain in your own words what 'Citizen Advocacy and the Legislative Process' refers to.
questions.a: The participatory pathway wherein civil society groups articulate social issues to prompt statutory enactments by parliamentarians.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Citizen Advocacy and the Legislative Process'.
questions.a: Statutory evolution often commences with civilian campaigns that compel Parliament to address urgent social grievances.

concepts.title: Popular Resistance to Arbitrary and Repressive Laws

questions.q: Using the method 'Popular Resistance to Arbitrary and Repressive Laws', work with: media_criticism = 45, peaceful_boycotts = 100, public_meetings = 10. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of civil_resistance.

Take the relation taught for 'Popular Resistance to Arbitrary and Repressive Laws' and work with: media_criticism = 4, peaceful_boycotts = 300, public_meetings = 40. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of civil_resistance.
Explain in your own words what 'Popular Resistance to Arbitrary and Repressive Laws' refers to.
questions.a: Civil dissent exercised by citizens against statutes that are formally valid yet perceived as unjust, inequitable, or repressive.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Popular Resistance to Arbitrary and Repressive Laws'.
questions.a: Democratic engagement extends beyond polling day to active resistance against unfair legislative actions.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Popular Resistance to Arbitrary and Repressive Laws', in plain ASCII form.
Explain in your own words what 'Judicial Review of Unconstitutional Legislation' refers to.
questions.a: The constitutional authority of independent courts to alter, strike down, or invalidate enactments violating constitutional norms.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Judicial Review of Unconstitutional Legislation'.
questions.a: The judiciary acts as a final safeguard ensuring all parliamentary legislation complies with foundational constitutional guarantees.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Judicial Review of Unconstitutional Legislation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: judicial_action = strike_down if law_contravenes_constitution else uphold
